text:
Ana: Quick heads-up — reproduced a mobile case where TCP drops mid-stream, client reconnects and the gateway ends up replaying from the start. Result: duplicated tokens and doubled billing for the user. Logs attached below.

Mike: Ugh. Any correlation id or request-id in logs?

Ana: Yes, request-id=rid_9f3a. Snippet: 
```
2026-02-12T18:04:21Z gateway: stream-start rid=rid_9f3a client=mobile-83
2026-02-12T18:04:28Z gateway: conn-reset client=mobile-83 errno=ECONNRESET
2026-02-12T18:04:29Z gateway: reconnect start rid=rid_9f3a new-conn=conn-234
2026-02-12T18:04:29Z edge: replaying request rid=rid_9f3a from=0
2026-02-12T18:04:40Z billing: tokens=300 rid=rid_9f3a
```

Dina: Sounds like we need a resumable-resume-lite protocol for thin clients. Keep it simple: client sends last-seen token offset + short resume token. Edge answers accept/restart. No transaction logs, just checkpoint mapping to a short window in an LRU store.

Mike: We tried full streaming checkpoints before; memory cost exploded. How do we bound this cheaply?

Kevin: Bound it with three controls: TTL (e.g., 30s), max tokens checkpointed (e.g., 1024), and shard-local LRU eviction. Store only (resume-token -> last-offset, model-variant, partial-kv-hash). Resume contains token and offset, server verifies compatibility. If mismatch -> restart.

Dina: Example header sketch: 
```
Client -> Edge:
  POST /v1/generate
  Headers:
    X-Resume-Token: "sha256:abc123"   # optional; opaque to client
    X-Last-Offset: "512"              # last token index client saw

Edge -> Client (on reconnect):
  200 Resume-Accepted
  X-Resume-Mode: "token-window"    # or "restart"
```
If Resume-Accepted, gateway streams starting from offset and backend replays only suffix.

Ana: Two concerns: 1) billing correctness: we must not charge twice for replayed tokens; 2) side-effects / non-idempotent steps when model has stateful tool calls.

Mike: For billing we can emit a single `billing:resumed=true` event and prorate tokens only for new tokens beyond last-offset. Need to audit existing billing pipeline for resumed flag.

Kevin: For side-effects, use a conservative policy: only allow resume for requests marked idempotent (client-specified) or those with no tool-call side-effects detected by evals. Otherwise gateway should reply `restart-required`. We can add `X-Resume-Allowed: true|false` at request time.

Dina: Also need observability: counters for resume_attempts, resume_accepts, resume_restarts, resume_window_evictions. Surface per-model variant so we can correlate regressions.

ops-bot: Suggested alert rules: resume_accept_rate < 95% for >5m, and resume_evictions/sec > 10 -> paging to infra on-call. Metric names: `edge.resume.attempts`, `edge.resume.accepts`, `edge.resume.evictions`.

Mike: Implementation plan: prototype gateway-only flow (no backend changes) that uses `X-Last-Offset` + opaque resume token, edge keeps minimal mapping and asks backend to stream from offset if supported. If backend lacks resume support, edge translates to `restart`. I'll spike a PoC and limit rollout to mobile clients behind a feature flag.

Ana: Awesome. Can you add a small RFC follow-up doc with tradeoffs: memory, billing, security (resume token replay/reforging), and fallback semantics? Punt long-term stateful tool handling to an eval.

Kevin: Also: version the headers early (`X-Resume-Version: 1`) so client/server negotiation is explicit. Race conditions with canaries are nasty if formats change.

Dina: +1. Adding a short example of token handshake to the RFC will help implementers.

Mike: I'll open a draft PR and RFC stub. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/987 (draft). Spiking next week.

Ana: Thanks — please tag infra + billing when PR goes up. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Noted. Scheduling follow-up sync: #eng-architecture calendar invite pending.
